hints: Focus on what a termination step really is, two radicals joining together to make a neutral molecule with no new radical.
List the carbon radicals you can actually get from propane, the primary $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\cdot$ and the secondary $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}\cdot\text{CH}_3$.
Try joining those C3 radicals in pairs and count the carbon skeleton to see which C6 branched alkanes can form and which cannot.
walkthrough:
**Recall what termination means**

Termination ends the chain by removing radicals. Two radicals combine to give a stable molecule.

$$ \text{R}\cdot + \text{R}'\cdot \rightarrow \text{R-R}' $$

**Identify the propyl radicals**

Propane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Removing one H gives only two possibilities.

$$ \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\cdot \text{ (n-propyl, primary)} $$
$$ \text{CH}_3\text{CH}\cdot\text{CH}_3 \text{ (isopropyl, secondary)} $$

**Combine them in pairs**

Join the radical carbons together to make a $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$ alkane.

$$ \text{n-propyl + isopropyl} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 $$
$$ \text{isopropyl + isopropyl} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 $$

**Check molecule 1**

Molecule 1 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, 3-methylpentane. This needs a C2 fragment and a C4 fragment joined, which are not the C3 radicals from propane, so it cannot form this way.

options.A: States 1, 2 and 3 are all possible. Statements 2 and 3 are correct but 1 is not, so this combination is false.
options.B: States 1 and 2 only are possible. Statement 2 is correct as isopropyl + isopropyl combination, but 1 cannot be made from two C3 propyl radicals and 3 is missed.
options.C: States 2 and 3 only are possible. 3 is n-propyl + isopropyl giving 2-methylpentane, and 2 is isopropyl + isopropyl giving 2,3-dimethylbutane. 1 would require different radicals, so 2 and 3 only is correct.
options.D: States 1 only is possible. 1 is 3-methylpentane and cannot be formed by combining two C3H7 radicals from propane, so this is false.
